data.headline: Principal Engineer at Epic Games
data.about:
I am a natural born techie having developed a love for computers since a very young age. I successfully "killed" my first computer at the age of 6 when I was playing around in the Command Prompt and accidentally ran DELTREE from the root directory. Since then I had wanted to become a computer programmer for most of my life, learning how to code in my free time. I took every programming and technology class I could during high school and learned core networking components there as well. I also started using Linux almost exclusively in high school, becoming very familiar with the terminal and rebuilding my personal computer when it would break, which it often would as I was prone to hacking around. 

Learning on my own throughout my entire life has given me a keen sense of work ethic and character. Teaching myself to be motivated and dedicated to my passions and what I want to learn has propelled me fairly far in my career. 

My most proud accomplishment to date are the several patches accepted into the Linux kernel that I have submitted. This was a great opportunity to teach myself the C programming language, and also taught me how to stay motivated in a project, even in spite of failures and setbacks.

description.text:
Software Engineer on Terraform Ecosystem

* Wrote, maintained, implemented bug fixes for Terraform in Golang
* Split-out provider plugins into separate software projects to aid in decreasing developer overhead
* Wrote Golang SDK for Oracle Public Cloud
* Wrote Terraform Provider Plugin for Oracle Public Cloud
* Made over 4k individual contributions to the Terraform and supporting providers

* Use modern Hashicorp tools to improve Atlas reliability
* Improve scaling, throughput, and uptime of internal services
* Help increase developer happiness, by decreasing deployment time
* Perform on-call duties to ensure maximum availability
* Improve upon various internal Go services
* Develop, test, and engineer new operational solutions

• Configure systems for development, test and production of a scalable consumer and e- commerce Internet website.
• Monitor and tune systems stability, capacity and performance. • Scale infrastructure to meet demand.
• Troubleshoot system issues as necessary
• Ensure system and network security
• Partner with development team in supporting new features and services
• On-call duties for production server issues and outages

While working at The Data Cave I performed routine daily administration tasks to ensure that our services were running constantly for our customers. I rebuilt our whole infrastructure during my first four months of employment and have built everything from the ground up. While working at The Data Cave, I became very familiar with virtualization, server administration, and automated configuration management. I have also became very familiar with the networking layer of systems support. From configuring Cisco Switches, Routers, and Vyatta Routers, I have thoroughly improved my knowledge of networking, and continue to do so on a daily basis. 

I currently manage a small VM cluster containing several redundant Linux server instances spread out across multiple QEMU hypervisors. I implemented and fully monitor all of our internal services with a combination of Nagios and ComHub (An open-source Nagios Alert Wrangler that we wrote in-house). I also manage and maintain our redundant DNS, Cacti, NTP, and LDAP servers. I currently use Ansible to provision and automate the build process of our VM's, yet have begun to implement Chef as an automated configuration management tool. 

The biggest asset that I have learned from The Data Cave is to respect our production environment. I learned how to place uptime and customer availability of our services at a high priority to ensure complete transparency across our connectivity platform.

While working at Analytical Engineering I had the great opportunity to develop C++ applications with an amazing team of talented individuals. I wrote, tested, distributed, and maintained a fairly large C++ codebase using SVN for version control. I contributed to several projects during my employment there and even started and finished several new projects. We ran all of our applications on Gentoo Linux, and I served as a Linux Administrator as well as a developer. Installing, maintaining, and repairing the Linux Systems gave me a lot of experience in high stress situations. 

One of the most crucial tools that I learned from working at Analytical Engineering was how to debug and fix software. While our company was a service company, the service could not be done if our software did not work. This taught me how to quickly debug and troubleshoot any software issues that arose, and quickly implement a fix or bug report to fix at a later time. 

Analytical Engineering is also a sister company of The Data Cave, so when The Data Cave lost their previous Systems Administrator I had proven myself capable enough to be promoted to that position.

While working at Central Computer Repair I directly interfaced with customers and clients, assisting them in various computer repair issues. I would travel remote as well as work locally in the shop, and thoroughly repair customer computers. I became fairly proficient at virus removal, malware removal, registry errors, diagnosing hardware errors, fixing hardware errors, and direct customer interactions. 

I worked on mainly windows desktops and laptops, but also was able to service Linux and Apple machines as well. During my employment with Central Computer Repair, I also worked directly with several customers to create custom computer builds for them, working continuously to ensure the customer was pleased with my work.
